title: Spatial Rhythm, Grouping & Layout
principle: A spacing scale supplies the vocabulary. Spatial rhythm determines how that vocabulary is composed.

relationship_order.intent: Two elements form one immediate reading or interaction unit.
relationship_order.use_when: Separating the elements would make the unit harder to understand.
failure_signals: The pair looks like separate controls or facts.
Another nearby element appears more closely related.

relationship_order.intent: Elements are distinct but directly explain or operate on one another.
relationship_order.use_when: The relationship should be clear before the user reads labels or borders.
examples: input and help or error text
failure_signals: Supporting text appears to belong to the next item.
A control appears detached from the content it affects.

relationship_order.intent: Peer items belong to the same collection, task, or repeated pattern.
relationship_order.use_when: Users should scan the items as a coherent set while still distinguishing each item.
examples: one form field to the next
failure_signals: Repeated peers use visibly different gaps without a reason.
Items merge into one dense block.

relationship_order.intent: Groups are related within the same region but perform different roles.
relationship_order.use_when: The user needs a visible pause before switching subtask or content type.
failure_signals: Different subtasks appear to be one group.
Every gap has equal emphasis and the layout feels monotonous.

relationship_order.intent: Major regions need the strongest pause in the page rhythm.
relationship_order.use_when: The user is moving to a new topic, stage, or page-level responsibility.
examples: one page section to the next
failure_signals: Major regions are hard to identify when scanning.
Large empty areas interrupt a flow without communicating a boundary.

principles.name: Preserve relational order
principles.guidance: Resolve relationship ranks with the product's own tokens so closer relationships never receive more space than looser relationships without an explicit reason.
principles.validation: Check that attached < associated < grouped < separated < sectional in the rendered context. Ranks describe ordering, not ratios or pixel multipliers.

principles.name: Use repetition to create rhythm
principles.guidance: Repeated peers should use the same spatial pattern. Predictability makes collections easier to scan.
principles.validation: Compare repeated instances and flag unexplained changes in internal padding, sibling gaps, or alignment.

principles.name: Use variation to create hierarchy
principles.guidance: Not every gap should be equal. Deliberate changes in space create pauses, transitions, and emphasis.
principles.validation: Check that major group and section boundaries remain distinguishable without relying only on borders or colour.

principles.name: Let content and typography lead
principles.guidance: Choose the scale and rhythm for the actual type, content length, controls, language, platform, and user context. A baseline grid is a guide, not a universal law.
principles.validation: Test realistic content, text resizing, translated strings, and multiple viewport widths rather than empty placeholders.

principles.name: Let the layout context own external spacing
principles.guidance: Parents should normally control gaps between siblings; components should control their internal padding. This prevents leftover margins and accidental double spacing.
principles.validation: Inspect whether parent gap and child margins combine to create unintended space.

principles.name: Permit accountable optical adjustment
principles.guidance: Visual weight, icons, type metrics, and irregular shapes can require a supported neighbouring token or a documented exception.
principles.validation: Require a short reason for exceptions and review the rendered result; do not fail a layout merely because every measurement is not mathematically identical.

patterns.name: Form stack
patterns.description: A vertical sequence of labels, controls, supporting messages, fields, and actions.

relationships.rationale: The label identifies the control.
The message explains the control's value or state.
Fields are peers in one task.
Actions complete or leave the data-entry task.

rhythm: Keep labels and messages visually attached to their own control.
Repeat the same field rhythm unless a subgroup or conditional region needs a deliberate pause.
Do not use a universal gap between every direct child of the form.
responsive_behavior: Preserve relationship order when the form becomes single-column.
Allow wrapping and text expansion without detaching messages from their controls.
manual_review: Can each help or error message be assigned to the correct field by position alone?
Do the actions read as the end of the form rather than another field?

patterns.name: Settings section
patterns.description: Related preferences grouped under headings, with controls that affect nearby descriptions or values.

relationships.rationale: The description qualifies the setting.
The control affects the named setting.
Rows are peers within one settings category.
Categories represent page-level responsibility changes.

rhythm: Repeat row rhythm within a category.
Use a stronger pause between categories than between rows.
Keep controls visually inside the region they affect.
responsive_behavior: When a row stacks on a small viewport, keep its control nearer to its own copy than to the next row.
Do not preserve desktop alignment by creating large, irregular mobile gaps.
manual_review: Does every control clearly belong to one setting?
Can users scan category boundaries without reading every heading?

patterns.name: Card collection
patterns.description: Repeated cards that form a collection while maintaining a smaller rhythm inside each card.

relationships.rationale: The description explains the title.
Actions are related to the card but play a different role.
Cards are peers in one collection.
The collection ends before a new page topic begins.

rhythm: Keep repeated card padding and internal patterns consistent.
Avoid making the gap between cards indistinguishable from the padding inside cards.
Treat equal card heights as a layout choice, not a reason to introduce arbitrary internal voids.
responsive_behavior: Preserve internal rhythm as the grid changes column count.
Review the vertical rhythm after cards become a single stack.
manual_review: Is it immediately clear what belongs inside each card?
Do repeated cards feel like peers rather than individually improvised layouts?

patterns.name: Editorial flow
patterns.description: Headings, paragraphs, lists, media, captions, callouts, and references in reading order.

relationships.rationale: A heading belongs more strongly to what follows than to the previous section.
Paragraphs continue one reading flow.
The caption identifies or explains the media.
A new heading begins a new topic or level of the argument.

rhythm: Coordinate line height, paragraph spacing, and heading margins as one reading rhythm.
Keep a heading closer to the content it introduces than to the content it concludes.
Use callouts as purposeful interruptions, not random changes of spacing.
responsive_behavior: Allow type and large sectional spaces to breathe with the viewport where appropriate.
Keep line length and page gutters in balance with the spatial scale.
manual_review: Does the reading flow have clear pauses without becoming fragmented?
Do captions and notes remain attached to the correct content after reflow?

patterns.name: Dashboard
patterns.description: Dense data, controls, summaries, and regions with different priorities and update frequencies.

relationships.rationale: The value is meaningless without its label.
The title defines the panel's scope.
Controls should appear to operate on the nearby region.
Regions contain different analytical or operational responsibilities.

rhythm: Use compact repeated rhythms inside dense data regions and stronger pauses between responsibilities.
Do not make the whole page uniformly dense or uniformly spacious.
Keep the most important region legible through position, scale, and surrounding space rather than empty space alone.
responsive_behavior: Recompose regions when columns no longer fit; do not merely shrink every gap.
Preserve control-to-region association when panels move into a vertical order.
manual_review: Can users distinguish regional responsibilities at a glance?
Does dense content remain operable without erasing hierarchy?

density_modes.compact: Resolve the same relationship order to a tighter subset of the product scale. Preserve target-size and text-spacing requirements, and retain visible section boundaries.
density_modes.comfortable: Use the product's default mapping while maintaining clear contrast between internal, grouped, and sectional relationships.
density_modes.spacious: Resolve the same relationship order to more generous tokens without stretching attached pairs or fragmenting a task.

viewport_modes.small: Protect attached and associated relationships first. Recompose columns, then reduce larger group and section spaces only as needed.
viewport_modes.medium: Use available width to clarify groups and gutters without assuming the large-screen composition fits unchanged.
viewport_modes.large: Allow stronger sectional pauses and wider gutters where they improve hierarchy; avoid arbitrary empty areas that break task flow.
viewport_modes.fluid: Interpolate project tokens or semantic aliases where appropriate, while preserving relationship order across the supported viewport range.

token_resolution.instruction: Map the ordered relationships to the product's existing primitive or semantic spacing tokens. Do not infer a universal base unit, fixed ratio, or mandatory pixel value from this standard.
token_resolution.fallback: If no product scale exists, propose a small illustrative scale, label it as a project hypothesis, and validate it with realistic content and rendered review before adoption.
token_resolution.exception_policy: Prefer a supported neighbouring token for optical correction. If a raw value is necessary, record the affected pair, reason, viewport, and review evidence.

normative: WCAG 2.2 target-size and spacing requirements apply to pointer targets.
WCAG 2.2 text-spacing requirements test whether user overrides cause loss of content or functionality.
supplemental_accessibility_guidance: W3C cognitive accessibility guidance recommends white space to clarify chunks and reduce overwhelming presentation.
design_guidance: Relationship ranks, rhythm patterns, density guidance, and optical adjustment are design guidance rather than WCAG conformance requirements.
